The RFP, managed by RVK, covers custody, accounting, valuation, tax, corporate actions, derivatives, cash/STIF, FX, reporting and technology; performance analytics, alternatives, securities lending, optional benefit payments and transition support. It describes current operational complexity, including lagged alternative-asset accounting and daily reconciliations, with monthly reporting schedules. The RFP sets the process timeline, contacts and requirements for a signed cover letter and affirmations, service approach, completed questionnaire, transparent pricing, proposed contract and supporting samples. Proposals were due February 2, 2024, by email; questions were due January 12. Submission, communications, public-records, validity and contract rules are specified. SBCERS may amend, reject or negotiate proposals. Evaluation weights scope and credentials, services and technology, response quality, and fees; finalists may face interviews and due diligence.

nodes.title: 01_SBCERS Custody RFP - Final (Updated) (intro)
nodes.summary: Santa Barbara County Employees’ Retirement System (SBCERS) seeks proposals for global custody and related services. The RFP was issued January 8, 2024; questions were due January 12, responses scheduled for January 22, and submissions due February 2. Designated contacts are Jonathan Kowolik and Lindsey Longwell of RVK, Inc. The RFP covers SBCERS background and purpose, current asset and service arrangements and their complexity, and the service scope: organizational resources, technology and staffing; custody; cash/STIF management; foreign exchange; performance measurement and analytics; alternative investments; securities lending; optional benefit payments; and transition support. It sets a timeline, required proposal information (cover letter, service summary and questionnaire, pricing, contract affirmation, and additional materials), response requirements, and evaluation process. Separate materials include complexity details, contract terms, scope and contract affirmations, a technical questionnaire covering organizational, staffing, account, technology, custody, cash, FX, analytics, compliance, alternatives, lending, optional benefit-payment, and transition topics, plus pricing tables.

nodes.title: SECTION I – INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE
nodes.summary: Introduces SBCERS, established in 1944 to provide benefits to County employees and 11 contracting employers, and its OPEB/401(h) trust, closed to members joining from December 31, 2018; September 2023 assets were about $4.06 billion and $53 million. RVK manages the RFP. The RFP seeks global custody and related accounting, analytics and services, with securities-lending continuation or cessation scenarios and possible asset restructuring. Responses inform selection and due diligence, but SBCERS may negotiate, reject responses or withdraw; Addendum I details accounts, assets and operations. Scope covers secure, integrated, cost-effective custody, accounting, valuation, tax, corporate actions, derivatives, FX, cash, reporting, technology, records and support. Performance services include fee-based reporting, analytics, custom composites, benchmarks, compliance testing and historical data transitions. Alternative-investment services cover transactions, verified wires, notices, account setup, reconciliation and valuations. Securities lending requirements address collateral, controls, reporting, access and benchmarking. Optional benefit payments cover transition, payment processing, tax, reconciliation and online services. Proposals must address appendices, contract terms and transparent pricing for lending scenarios, without affiliated-provider or balance requirements.

nodes.title: A. Background
nodes.summary: Established in 1944, the Santa Barbara Employees’ Retirement System (SBCERS) provides retirement, disability, death, and survivor benefits to County of Santa Barbara employees and 11 contracting employers, including the Superior Court and ten special districts. SBCERS also administers an Other Post-Employment Benefit (OPEB) or 401(h) retiree health trust, established in September 2008 and closed to members joining SBCERS on or after December 31, 2018. As of September 30, 2023, SBCERS held approximately $4.06 billion in assets and the OPEB Plan approximately $53 million. RVK, Inc. manages the RFP process and related communications and activities.

nodes.title: B. Purpose of RFP
nodes.summary: The RFP seeks a qualified firm to provide SBCERS global custody, accounting, performance measurement/analytics, and related services. Bidders should address securities-lending scenarios: continuation, continuation with guideline changes, or cessation. SBCERS is also considering restructuring OPEB and Retirement Plan assets into investable Master Trust Units held by OPEB. Responses will inform finalist selection, due diligence, and possible Investment Committee review and approval. SBCERS may negotiate, conduct future due diligence, use ideas from responses, reject any or part of responses, or withdraw the RFP without selecting a contractor. Addendum I details current account, asset, composite, and service complexity, including accounting, performance/analytics and compliance deliverables; assets and transactions by market; accounting and performance schematics; FX execution methods and currency pairs; securities-lending parameters; and lendable assets.

nodes.title: D. Scope of Services
nodes.summary: SBCERS seeks cost-effective global custody and related accounting, performance analytics, technology, automation, and vendor integration for traditional, alternative, synthetic, lagged, and current valuations. The provider must offer experienced, responsive, stable staff; dedicated transition support; interoperable systems and manager interfaces; training; secure, resilient operations; eight-year electronic records; audited reporting; issue resolution and client education. Core services include global custody, settlement, trade-date GAAP accounting, tax monitoring and reclaims, optional class actions, proxy communications and voting records, asset-wide accounting, corporate actions, derivatives, FX, independent pricing and fair valuation, regulatory support, fee payments, rebalancing, reporting, online data, scorecards, reconciliation, price-challenge investigation, trade monitoring, and secure third-party links. Benefit payments are optional; alternative cash flows and valuation enrichment remain with Hamilton Lane. Cash services include projections, competitively priced sweeps and overnight deposits with cost disclosure, secure wires, and monthly authorization audits; custody pricing must be separate from asset-management mandates. FX services include dealer trading, automated repatriation, execution disclosures, third-party venue flexibility, capped or non-incremental fees, and transparent client-directed transfers.

nodes.title: A. Organizational Resources, Technology, & Staffing
nodes.summary: SBCERS seeks proposals for cost-effective global custody and related services, including accounting and performance analytics, advanced technology, automated solutions, and integration with its other vendors. Support must address lagged/non-lagged valuations and traditional, alternative, and synthetic exposures; details appear in Addendum I. Benefit payments remain internal but are listed as optional, while alternative-investment cash-flow processing and valuation enrichment remain with Hamilton Lane. The provider must offer best-in-class service through a knowledgeable, responsive, low-turnover team and dedicated support for transfers and restructuring. Requirements include a strong record serving sophisticated asset owners; timely SOC reports; accessible, interoperable systems, manager interfaces, complete transaction histories, and standard reports; conversion and ongoing training; robust information security, backups, disaster recovery, and system availability; eight-year electronic record retention and consistent audited reporting. Staff must be technically capable, accessible, proactive, responsive, trained, and effective at resolving issues, communicating with stakeholders, tracking metrics, and proposing feasible solutions; SBCERS staff must also receive invitations to client conferences and education sessions.

nodes.title: B. Core Custodial Services
nodes.summary: The provider must deliver domestic and global securities custody, clearing and delivery-versus-payment settlement; GAAP trade-date accounting; tax-liability monitoring, active reclaim and claim pursuit, and annual reclaim-status reporting; optional class-action services; secure electronic data access and maximum straight-through processing. It must deliver security-holder communications, act on voting instructions, and report voting records. Accounting covers all portfolio assets and transactions, corporate actions, derivatives, foreign exchange, and lagged or current alternatives; uses fiscal-year, cost and average-cost-basis conventions; and provides updated market values, independent pricing controls and fair-valuation procedures. Services include monthly audited and daily best-available accounting, regulatory-reporting support, directed fee payments, rebalancing, standard asset classifications, and multi-source corporate-action notices. Monthly reports are due by the eleventh business day, with daily production scorecards and online data. The provider and managers must reconcile holdings, cash, income, accruals and values, investigate differences and price challenges, and enable monitoring of forecasts, holdings and trades. Secure third-party data links and accounting reports in agreed formats, including external-manager NAV reconciliation, are required.

nodes.title: C. Cash/STIF Management
nodes.summary: The provider must deliver daily cash-flow projections and management reports to SBCERS and outside managers; offer competitively priced cash-sweep options with varying risk objectives, including optional balance-sheet deposits, and disclose related fees, revenue, and costs; and provide and disclose costs for overnight deposits after the sweep deadline. Core and value-added custody services must be priced independently of asset-management mandates. The provider must send and receive domestic and international wires, secure and authenticate transfers and disbursements according to SBCERS requirements, and provide monthly audit reports of online cash directions submitted and approved by SBCERS staff.

nodes.title: D. Foreign Exchange
nodes.summary: The custodian must provide SBCERS and outside investment managers with dealer-traded foreign exchange and an automated standing-instruction repatriation program, with at least annual disclosures on policies, procedures, rate competitiveness, and execution methods. It must support managers using third-party currency venues when they opt out of the standing-instruction program and, where within its control and capabilities and allowed by law, not prevent trades with other providers. Third-party currency transaction fees may not be incremental, or must be capped at the domestic settlement fee. Client-directed transfers in U.S. dollars and foreign currencies must be available, with associated costs transparent, reasonable, and disclosed.

nodes.title: E. Investment Performance Measurement and Analytics
nodes.summary: SBCERS’ accounts/composites and assigned benchmarks will be maintained in a centralized listing updated at least monthly. Performance reporting will be gross and net of fees using CFA Institute-compliant methods, with schedules and formats detailed in the contract. Deliverables include a daily online portal with current and historical analytics; detailed monthly market and portfolio reports; monthly equity characteristics and fixed-income attribution; and quarterly total-plan attribution, with specified reports due by the 13th business day after month-end. Providers must support flexible custom composites and additional daily, monthly, and annual reports. Monthly compliance testing services include collaboratively designed tests and reports, ongoing test updates, annual procedures and validation, offline calculations for tests beyond system capabilities, and online report and alert access with training. If providers transition, the incoming non-incumbent must back-load performance data for all open and closed accounts and composites, and standard and custom benchmarks.

nodes.title: F. Alternative Investment Services
nodes.summary:
F. Alternative Investment Services
1. Provider shall process all transactions related to SBCERS’ associated alternative investment accounts.
2. Provider shall make a call back to SBCERS to confirm wire information and submit wire instructions SBCERS for approval to process accurate and timely funding transactions.
3. Provider shall be an interested party on all alternative investment contribution and distribution notices and will independently obtain all monthly / quarterly financial statements from General Partners.
4. Provider shall set up and maintain any new alternative investment accounts including the following key attributes: Vintage Year, Investment Type, Deal Commitment, Date of Commitment, Deal Currency, and Fund Manager.
5. Provider shall maintain and reconcile partnership valuations.
6. Provider shall calculate roll-forward valuations and coordinate pricing activity with accounting unit prior to monthly deadlines.
Santa Barbara County Employees’ Retirement System Global Custody and Related Services 15

nodes.title: G. Custodial Securities Lending Services
nodes.summary: The provider must support either continued securities lending—with overnight-repo cash collateral reinvestment and traditional non-cash collateral—or cessation, and price custodial and related services for both scenarios. SBCERS may stop lending and control eligible securities and quantities, and approve borrowers. Domestic and international loans, including accrued interest, require collateral of 102% and 105% of fair value, respectively; collateral must be marked to market daily, with deficiencies corrected within 24 hours before relending or extension. The provider must deliver electronic daily, monthly, quarterly, and annual account-level reports of activity, income, expenses, average and period-end loan volumes, and total income; reports and earnings credits are due within 10 business days after month-end. Staff and authorized parties must have online prior-business-day reporting access and professional support. At least quarterly, the provider must report benchmark comparisons, including utilization, lending, reinvestment, and returns on lent and lendable assets, using DataLend or a comparable source.

nodes.title: H. (At SBCERS Option) Benefit Payment Services
nodes.summary: The SBCERS optional benefit-payment service requires conversion from existing platforms with at least two parallel payment cycles; experienced support staff and backups; automated trustee/custodian and staff interfaces; reconciled DDA services with disclosed float policies; and secure, accurate processing of monthly pension payments, twice-monthly lump sums, tax reporting/notices and filing, refunds, stop-payments/reissues, and pensioner updates. A secure online portal must provide transaction histories, reports, balances, payee data, tax forms, and customary reports; standard reports must include available historical payment activity. A reverse feed must support monthly reconciliation. Providers must submit detailed transition plans; incumbents must describe retention and relationship enhancements and any service-transition rollout. Addendum I details scope and assets; proposals must affirm scope and contract terms using Appendices 1 and 2, answer Appendix 3, and provide Appendix 4 pricing for bundled custody under securities-lending continuation and cessation scenarios. Pricing must use stated units, reconcile supplemental estimates, and disclose incremental fees. Proposals cannot depend on using an affiliated investment provider or maintaining balances with one.

nodes.title: SECTION III – REQUIRED INFORMATION
key_items: A. Cover Letter; B. Summary of Proposed Services; C. Services Questionnaire
E. Contract Terms and Conditions Affirmation
nodes.summary: Section III requires: (A) a cover letter to the designated contact stating firm name, principal office, and authorized representative’s name, phone, and email; affirming capability, RFP review, acceptance of all RFP terms, and signatory authority to bind the Respondent; and including a signed scope affirmation (Appendix 1). (B) A clear, sufficiently detailed service approach under Section I-D, recommended additional tasks, plans for working with SBCERS, and required staff assistance. (C) Completed Appendix 3 questionnaires in electronic Word format by February 2, 2024, 6 PM ET. (D) Appendix 4 pricing in Excel and a pro-forma annual revenue estimate based on interpreted RFP volumes and proposed fees. (E) Signed PDF Appendix 2 contract affirmation, reference to Addendum II, and proposed agreements, including a redlined global custodian agreement incorporating agreed terms plus necessary appendices, schedules, and components; SBCERS may negotiate further. (F) Clearly labeled electronic sample materials: custody agreements; staff biographies; sub-custody network list; SOC 1 and SOC 2 reports; business continuity/disaster recovery plans and testing; pricing sources; inter-con flow chart; accounting/service-delivery diagram; custodial sweep vehicle details, performance, costs and guidelines; reporting samples; 2024 FTP cutoff calendar; and transition-planning documentation.

nodes.title: SECTION IV – RESPONSE REQUIREMENTS
nodes.summary: Respondents must submit complete, clearly formatted proposals answering every question, including required disclosures and attachments, by February 2, 2024, at 6 PM ET to investments@sbcers.org and IOSG@rvkinc.com, copying Rebecca Valdez and Rico Pardo. Respondents bear responsibility for timely delivery; late or misdirected submissions may be disqualified. Preparation and submission costs are not reimbursed, nor are expenses outside the compensation schedule. Questions and additional-information requests go in writing to IOSG@rvkinc.com through January 12; other RFP communications must go to Jonathan Kowolik and Lindsey Longwell at RVK. Do not contact SBCERS personnel about the RFP except through pre-existing business relationships. SBCERS and RVK do not guarantee outside information; revisions come by addendum. Proposals must reflect understanding of the work and remain valid at least 180 days. Materials may be disclosed under California public-records law; mark potentially exempt material clearly and separately, as blanket confidentiality claims do not prevent disclosure. SBCERS may reject proposals, amend or cancel the RFP, correct errors, waive defects, make partial awards, or seek clarifications, evidence of capability, interviews, or site visits. Submission accepts the RFP terms unless exceptions are stated and included in the final written contract; changes are generally prohibited. After selection, SBCERS may negotiate terms and fees or conduct further due diligence.

nodes.title: Proposal Response and Submission Requirements
nodes.summary: This section outlines the terms governing proposal submission and review. Respondents must follow the requested format, answer every question, provide required disclosures, and include relevant attachments. Complete electronic proposals are due February 2, 2024, by 6 PM ET, and must be sent to investments@sbcers.org and IOSG@rvkinc.com, with Rebecca Valdez and Rico Pardo copied. Respondents are responsible for timely delivery to the specified contacts; late submissions or delivery elsewhere may result in disqualification. SBCERS and RVK, Inc. are not liable for respondent costs incurred in preparing or submitting proposals or before a contract is issued. SBCERS will not pay expenses outside the applicable compensation schedule.

nodes.title: D. Additional Information
nodes.summary: RFP questions and additional-information requests must be sent in writing to IOSG@rvkinc.com; questions are accepted through January 12, 2024. Firms must not contact SBCERS employees, officers, or Trustees about the RFP, except through pre-existing business relationships, and other RFP communications must go to Jonathan Kowolik and Lindsey Longwell at RVK. SBCERS and RVK do not guarantee information from other sources; revisions will be issued to RFP recipients by addendum. Respondents must understand the specifications and work, and keep proposals valid for at least 180 days. Proposals may be disclosed under California’s Public Records Act; specific potentially exempt material should be clearly marked and separable, while blanket confidentiality labels do not prevent disclosure. Responses must be complete, clear, concise, and economical. SBCERS may reject any or all proposals without liability. After selection, it may negotiate contract terms, fees, and conditions or conduct further due diligence.

nodes.title: RFP Communications, Proposal Rules, and Presentation
nodes.summary: RFP correspondence must go to Jonathan Kowolik and Lindsey Longwell at RVK, except clarification questions and requests for additional information; questions are accepted through January 12, 2024, and no inquiries should go elsewhere. SBCERS and RVK do not guarantee information from other sources; any RFP revisions will be issued by addendum to recipients. Respondents should review the work and specifications, and proposals must remain valid for at least 180 days. Proposal materials may become public under the California Public Records Act after contract award. Potentially exempt material must be clearly labeled and separable; SBCERS will protect it only as legally permitted. Labeling an entire proposal confidential does not exempt it from disclosure. Responses must be complete and presented simply and economically, with clear, concise descriptions of capabilities and approach.

SBCERS (or its designate) will be the sole judge of the Respondent’s responsiveness to the RFP and reserves the right to reject any or all responses, with or without cause, without incurring any liability whatsoever.
I. Contract Execution or Further Due Diligence
After selection, SBCERS may enter into contract negotiations with the selected Respondent to finalize terms, fees and conditions. Alternatively, at the sole

nodes.title: J. Further Instructions and Conditions
nodes.summary: RFP responses must follow all instructions or risk rejection. Submitting a proposal accepts the RFP’s terms unless specific exceptions are stated and confirmed in the final contract. SBCERS solely controls the schedule and sequence, may amend or cancel the RFP before the deadline, and may reject respondents in default of prior contracts or for misrepresentation. Written contracts supersede alleged oral agreements. SBCERS may correct clerical errors in awards and reject proposals that limit or alter RFP terms or specifications. Respondents must provide evidence of relevant experience, capability, facilities, and financial standing when requested. Proposal changes after submission are generally prohibited, except qualifying corrections or omissions; SBCERS may request clarifications at the respondent’s expense. SBCERS may make partial awards, reject any or all proposals in whole or part, and waive technical defects, irregularities, or omissions when it judges this serves its best interests.

nodes.title: SECTION V – EVALUATION PROCESS
nodes.summary: SBCERS and RVK will score proposals using written responses, requested information, and any interviews: scope, servicing and credentials (30%); core/value-added services and technology (40%); response quality and capability evidence (5%); and fees relative to service quality (25%). SBCERS need not choose the lowest-cost bidder. Finalists may be invited to headquarters interviews or on-site presentations and due diligence, asked for references and detailed capability information, and required to submit best-and-final fees; performance-based compensation may be considered but is optional. The addendum reports holdings and accounts as of September 30, 2023, totaling $4.112 billion, with 33 accounts and 224 non-cash line-item holdings; 12 alternative-asset accounts use monthly or quarterly lagged accounting. Daily unaudited NAV accounting includes cash and asset reconciliations, accrual, income, corporate-action, and pricing reviews. Monthly final reports are available on the 11th business day, with audited reports closed on the 10th.

result.title: 02_SBCERS Custody RFP - Addendum I - MS Excel
result.summary: The January 2024 SBCERS custody RFP addendum describes 33 accounts holding about $4.112 billion, including lagged alternative assets, and specifies accounting services, reconciliations, reporting deadlines, performance accounts/composites and benchmarks, online analytics, custom reporting, and monthly compliance reports. It provides September 2023 asset, holdings, transaction-volume, and account-schematic data for Retirement and OPEB investments, plus a detailed performance-account hierarchy mapping managers, balances, weights, benchmarks, and inception dates. It reports 12-month FX volumes and deal counts by execution method and currency pair; securities-lending guidelines, collateral, on-loan balances, and a detailed inventory of lendable securities; and asset and transaction totals across domestic and international markets. Addendum II sets out proposed custody-agreement terms, requiring a draft or identified exceptions, and addresses account establishment, authorized instructions, foreign subcustodians, professional care, safekeeping and segregation, transaction and income processing, corporate actions, settlement, reporting, reconciliation, and prudent subcustodian selection and monitoring.

nodes.title: Accounting Key Service Deliverables
nodes.summary: The January 8, 2024 SBCERS custody-services addendum reports holdings as of September 30, 2023: 33 accounts and $4.112 billion across cash, domestic and global separate accounts, single- and multi-line commingled funds, and residuals; 12 alternative-asset accounts use monthly or quarterly lagged accounting. Account details are in the Acct-Schematic tab. Accounting services include daily unaudited NAV support through cash and asset reconciliations, accrual, income, corporate-action, and pricing reviews; monthly final reports are available by the 11th business day, with audited reports closed by the 10th. The performance section lists account/composite and benchmark counts (21, 6, 32, 30, and 3; details in PA-Acct-Bmk), daily online performance and historical analytics, monthly reports, final reports by the 13th business day, flexible composites, and additional reporting on request. Compliance reports for the prior month are delivered by the 23rd business day.

nodes.title: SBCERS Custody Performance and Compliance Services
nodes.summary: The page outlines performance accounts, composites, benchmarks, and service deliverables for SBCERS’s global custody RFP. It lists 21 composites, 6 SA components, 32 CF/cash components, 30 monthly standard benchmarks, and 3 monthly custom benchmarks, with further details in the “PA-Acct-Bmk” tab. The custodian must provide an online portal with available daily performance and historical analytics, plus monthly reports covering market and portfolio performance at SBCERS’s requested level of detail or aggregation, including current and historical data. Final monthly reports are due by the 13th business day after month-end. Flexible composite structures and custom composite creation, maintenance, and reporting are expected, along with additional daily, monthly, and yearly reports as needed. Monthly compliance reports for the prior month-end are due on the 23rd business day.

nodes.title: SBCERS - Assets and Transactions Values at September 30, 2023
nodes.summary: Pages 3–4 of the SBCERS report show asset and transaction values as of September 30, 2023, with trailing-12-month volumes. The tables cover U.S. DTC/Fed, physical securities, line-item/administration-only and OPEB assets, plus holdings across numerous countries and markets. They report September 30 assets, holdings and total buys/sells, including a total asset value of $4,063,999,017. Custodial STIF/cash totals $45,204,626; an additional measure is the 12-month daily average for EB Short Term Investment. Other transaction volumes are listed for domestic and non-U.S. incoming/outgoing wires, margin wires, third-party and custodial FX, futures buys/sells and margin paydowns, ETD transactions, receipt/delivery free, and outstanding reclaims.

It lists investment account names under the Retirement and OPEB plans, including domestic and international equity, fixed income, real estate, private equity and infrastructure, cash, and index accounts. The table reports account-level accrued amounts and market values, account types (such as line item, separate account, multi-line account, residuals, and cash account), holdings counts, and quarterly or monthly accounting indicators. nodes.title: SBCERS - Performance Account Schematic
nodes.summary: A multi-page SBCERS performance-account schematic maps the consolidated fund and investment composites to managers, component accounts, standard or custom benchmarks, market values, portfolio percentages, cash/cash-flow indicators, and inception dates. It reports total consolidation of about $4.02 billion (100%), with a later mapped total of about $4.01 billion (99.76%). The hierarchy includes total-fund policy and additional composites, then domestic and international equity, domestic and non-core fixed income, TIPS and other real-return assets, private equity, real estate, private infrastructure and natural resources, private credit, and cash/unallocated assets. Listed managers and accounts are paired with benchmarks such as Russell, MSCI, Bloomberg, Credit Suisse leveraged-loan, JP Morgan emerging-markets bond, CPI-plus, NCREIF, and custom composites. The tables also show category subtotals, individual account balances and weights—including small or negative cash positions—and associated benchmark and inception-date details.

nodes.title: SBCERS - Foreign Exchange Execution by Method and Currency Pair For Periods October 2022 through September 2023
nodes.summary: SBCERS’ foreign-exchange report covers October 2022–September 2023, listing USD volumes and deal counts by currency pair across three execution methods. Third-party non-custodial FX (negotiated, non-standing instruction) totaled $438,847,072 across 4,461 deals. The custodial standing-instruction defined-spread program covers freely convertible and restricted-market currencies, totaling $39,723,521 and 1,016 deals. Custodian-paired direct FX (negotiated, non-standing instruction) totaled $6,946,956 across 51 deals.

nodes.title: SBCERS - Securities Lending Program Parameters
nodes.summary: SBCERS participates in BNY Mellon’s agency securities-lending program and currently follows conservative collateral guidelines: cash collateral is held and invested in a separate account, with new investments limited to overnight repurchase agreements backed by traditional, non-equity collateral; non-cash collateral is limited to U.S. government debt and mortgages. Any future program would ideally retain these guidelines. The lendable portfolio, assuming unrestricted access to separate-account holdings, is listed on the “Lendable Assets” worksheet tab. Lending volumes have varied significantly. Monthly average on-loan figures for September 30, 2023, were $13,756,079.81 against cash collateral and $15,937,998.42 against non-cash collateral, totaling $29,694,078.23.

nodes.title: SBCERS - Separate Account Security Holdings for Lending Estimate at 9/30/2023
nodes.summary: SBCERS’ separate-account securities available for lending as of September 30, 2023, with reported market value plus accrued income of $1,033,746,461.86. The multi-page inventory lists security identifiers and descriptions, quantities, lendable-asset values, investment segments, and trade currencies. Holdings include fixed-income securities—corporate and government bonds, mortgage pools, and other debt—preferred securities, and equities. Issuers and markets span North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and other regions, across sectors such as utilities, energy, real estate, finance, industrials, technology, healthcare, and consumer goods. The table reports amounts in currencies including USD, CAD, EUR, GBP, AUD, JPY, and others.

nodes.title: Addendum II – CONTRACT TERMS AND CONDITIONS
nodes.summary: Addendum II lists standard custody-agreement terms that custodians must address in their RFP response: submit a draft agreement, identify any exceptions with alternative wording, or state that there are none. The terms appoint the custodian as bank and agent to establish and maintain an account holding the client’s transferred assets, with separate accounts managed by the client or appointed investment advisers authorized to transact by written instruction. The custodian must appoint foreign subcustodians for non-U.S. assets. It must provide services with the care, skill, diligence, and responsibility of a professional custodian, including safekeeping, segregation, corporate actions and class actions, settlement, income processing, transaction and price reporting, and reconciliation; this standard applies to services performed or omitted and to its representatives. Assets must be segregated from the custodian’s and other clients’ assets. The custodian is responsible for prudently selecting foreign subcustodians and monitoring whether those selections remain prudent.

result.title: 03_SBCERS Custody RFP - Addendum II - Contract Terms
key_items: Addendum II – CONTRACT TERMS AND CONDITIONS
result.summary: Addendum II provides standard custody-agreement terms for the RFP: establish client and adviser-managed accounts; define professional care, asset segregation, and foreign-subcustodian selection and oversight; govern authorized written instructions and key contacts; set custodian representations, UCC safeguards, and foreign-exchange terms; require records retention, proxy handling, and class-action monitoring, claims, reporting, and data access. It also addresses insurance, required notices, assistance with regulatory inquiries, sufficient cash without granting a lien, conflicts and self-dealing, confidentiality and information security, indemnification, assignment, termination and asset transfer, public-records disclosure and work-product ownership, California-law compliance, survival, and amendments. Custodians must identify exceptions and propose alternatives, or affirm none. Appendix 1 requires an authorized signer to affirm service-scope and RFP compliance and absence of material conflicts with SBCERS or its trustees, explain any exceptions, and provide signer and firm details, signature, and date.

key_items: IF NO IS ENTERED PLEASE FULLY DESCRIBE EXCEPTIONS, IF ANY, WITH REDLINE EDITS IN THE SPACE BELOW.
result.summary: Appendix 2 requires an authorized representative to affirm whether the respondent will include SBCERS’s Addendum II contract terms in the resulting agreement; any exceptions must be fully described with redline edits. Respondents must submit proposed agreements, incorporating agreed terms, required appendices, addenda, schedules, and other legal-agreement components. SBCERS may negotiate further. Signature details are requested. Appendix 3 begins a technical/services questionnaire covering corporate contact information; custody-service history and enhancements; ownership and affiliations; organizational changes and anticipated developments; custody assets, revenue share, and client count; key institutional needs and the firm’s ability to meet them; SBCERS’s relative client ranking by asset size, service scope, and staffing; business plans; relevant insurance; credit ratings; and custody-related litigation, regulatory sanctions, or proceedings over the past five years. The final question begins by asking about audits or investigations involving the company or affiliates by the Employee Benefit Security Administration, but is cut off.

result.title: 06_SBCERS Custody RFP - Appendix 3 - Technical Questionnaire
result.summary: The technical questionnaire assesses a custody provider’s organization, ownership, service record, financial and regulatory standing, references, third-party arrangements, client service, staffing, team continuity, and business plans. It requests client, account, asset, country, and sub-custodian statistics and detailed technology, systems, cybersecurity, privacy, continuity, and investment plans. Service questions cover custody and accounting controls, valuation, securities processing, tax, corporate actions, interfaces, reporting, alternative assets, and accounting integrations; cash sweeps, wires, overdrafts, and foreign exchange execution, pricing, disclosures, and netting; and performance, analytics, risk, compliance tools, data, and reporting. It also examines alternative-investment transaction and valuation support, securities-lending operations and safeguards, and optional pension benefit-payment services. Transition and conversion planning includes deconversion, teams, timelines, market moves, training, controls, and references. The appendix also requests executable pricing scenarios and fee schedules, including securities-lending revenue splits, collateral fees, assumptions, and asset-based rates.

nodes.title: A. Organization – Corporate
nodes.summary: The questionnaire requests corporate and service information from a trust/custody provider: primary contact details; service history and enhancements; ownership, affiliates and ownership percentages; significant past and anticipated organizational changes; custody assets, revenue share and client count; key institutional needs and the provider’s ability to meet them; SBCERS’s relative fit by asset size, service scope and staffing; and a three-to-five-year business plan. It also asks for relevant insurance, credit ratings, litigation, regulatory proceedings and audits or investigations, including outcomes and dates, plus references and standard custody agreements. Providers must explain how they monitor and improve service and communicate with clients. Any third-party or non-wholly-owned providers must be identified, with relationship type and duration, comparable client counts, management and quality controls, assurances of service continuity, and remedies if their services or reporting are unsatisfactory.

nodes.title: B. Professional Staff
nodes.summary: Requests details on professional staffing, including total headcount and job-function classifications; assigned personnel, dedicated status, other clients served, biographies, and related experience at other organizations; and a team roster showing titles, locations, tenure, and estimated SBCERS FTE allocation, including shared services. Asks how service, communications, primary contacts, backup coverage, continuity, and team stability will be managed; recent personnel turnover, distinguishing departures from internal transfers; anticipated hiring; recruitment and retention efforts and results; conduct standards and compliance enforcement; and training of replacements. Also asks which unit will serve external investment managers and how it will coordinate with client service staff, custody, accounting, performance, securities lending, and other teams, including coordination across locations and time zones.

nodes.title: C. Accounts and Assets
nodes.summary: Section C requests information on accounts and assets: (39) as of September 30, 2023, institutional asset-owner client counts/relationships and aggregate asset size by client type—corporate, public fund, Taft-Hartley/union, endowment/foundation, and other—and five asset-size bands, plus totals; (40) institutional trust/custody account counts and total custody asset values in USD at year-ends 2019–2022 and September 30, 2023; (41) accounts gained and lost in 2018–2022 and through September 30, 2023, with counts and market values at account initiation or termination; (42) each country where client assets are custodied and the directly used, contractually engaged depositories, agents, or sub-custodian banks in each market, listing all where multiple; and (43) as of September 30, 2023, total countries, directly contracted providers, and market value of foreign assets held for U.S. investors.

nodes.title: D. Technology
nodes.summary: A technology and cybersecurity due-diligence questionnaire covering the technology organization’s responsibilities, reporting lines, staffing and contractors; personnel counts; project prioritization and coordination; custody-service systems, processing capacity, architecture changes and competitive differentiators; client notification of system changes; and incident response, mitigation, escalation and executive risk oversight. It requests five-year technology investment, enhancements, revenue allocation, new products, and plans for the current and next five years. Security topics include access controls, remote access, security standards and updates, SOC 1/2 and cybersecurity reports, alternative assurance, business continuity and disaster recovery plans and test results, program reviews, outsourcing, breaches, cyber insurance and claims, periodic and independent assessments and penetration testing, CISO oversight, staff training, cyber-threat response, privacy policies and protection, storage and disposal of personal information, and advanced authentication. It also asks whether the firm sells information, software, research, databases, or other services to investment-related firms.

nodes.title: E. Custody and Accounting Services
nodes.summary: The questionnaire seeks details on custody and accounting services: legal/regulatory compliance, responsible oversight and client communications, asset safekeeping and segregation, registration changes, derivatives, and liability for processing errors. It covers foreign sub-custodian selection, oversight, issue resolution and termination; pricing sources, methods, frequency, valuation treatment, exceptions and disputes; proxy services and securities/bankruptcy claims, including former-client, externally held assets and third-party support. It asks about manager and external-custodian interfaces, reporting, instructions, reconciliation, trade processing and authorization controls; settlement performance, failed trades and foreign exchange; income accruals, accurate posting, foreign tax and reclaim procedures; corporate actions, validation and receivables write-offs. It requests accounting-unit/system diagrams and details on controls, GAAP, multicurrency processing, integrations, processing schedules, STEP, period closes, Acumatica, general-ledger support and accounting deadlines. It also addresses online access, data history, identifiers, alternative-asset services, derivative accounting, archiving and possible OPEB/master-trust restructuring experience and implementation decisions.

nodes.title: F. Cash Management
nodes.summary: The section requests details on automatically swept overnight U.S. investment vehicles, including their strategies, objectives, guidelines, performance measurement and results, fees, revenue sharing, and prospectuses. It asks how daily cash sweeps are managed and integrated with trust accounting and cash forecasts; how managers are notified of available cash and cash needs; how post-cutoff receipts, automated and manual procedures, fees, and client access to transaction, remittance, disbursement, and STIF calculation data are handled. It also asks about alternative cash investments, their sweep integration, fees, rates, and terms; overdraft interest rates and calculation; incoming and outgoing wire capabilities and limits; cash transaction cutoff times and flexibility; wire authentication, approvals, security, automation, and planned developments; and separate portfolio wire accounts or other ways to link cash transactions to individual portfolios.

nodes.title: G. Foreign Exchange
nodes.summary: The questions seek details on custodial and third-party FX services, competitive differentiation and rates, the rationale for offering FX, and execution standards, including best execution. They cover how restricted currencies are identified and priced; agent sub-custodian relationships, rate oversight, and related revenue; and support for contracted spot and forward trades, including operational versus regulatory market restrictions and prospective features. Respondents must explain disclosures and records for indirect, standing-instruction, and direct trades, including timestamps, benchmarks, reference rates, explicit spreads, and revenue earned. They must describe repatriation methods, pricing and documentation, clients’ ability to opt out, and crediting on contractual value dates for third-party receipts. Specific questions address indirect execution and settlement, direct-trading availability and future plans in Brazil, India, Taiwan, and South Korea; restricted-market pricing evidence and compensation; and any netting programs, including participating accounts, pricing, spreads, and process examples.

nodes.title: H. Performance and Analytics Services
nodes.summary: The text requests details on performance and analytics services: organizational scale, staffing, coverage hours, ratios, experience, geographic coordination, and analytical resources; product content, timeliness, formats, frequency, sample reports, tracked characteristics, delivery dates, and internal versus external development; online access, raw-data downloads, report customization, available analytics/databases, and history. It covers return and attribution methods, cash-flow and stop-the-clock handling, valuation accuracy, partial-period and dollar-weighted private-market returns, asset-class pricing, supported instruments, benchmarks and composites, reconciliation, account setup, holdings retention, data feeds, deadlines, and standard or fee-based risk and peer services. It also asks about transaction transfers, composite membership, data storage, automation, and technical support. Compliance questions address tool design and delivery; pre/post-trade monitoring and limitations; rule programming, fees, and training; testable parameters and classifications; prohibited lists; accounting integration and data timing; exchange tracking; customized, retained, scheduled, online, and printable reports; security- and fund-level testing; and vendors, licenses, data fees, and client support.

nodes.title: K. Custodial Securities Lending Support Services
nodes.summary: A questionnaire on custodial securities lending covering program history, distinctive services, organizational structure and changes, client and relationship counts, program size and utilization, staffing and locations, and lending strategies. It requests five years of lendable assets, loans, and intrinsic spreads by asset class. It asks about failed trades, buy-ins, settlement responsibility and protections; past losses and mitigation; client safeguards and indemnification, including cash-in-lieu and collateral investment losses. It also covers credit reviews, borrower limits and approved brokers; collateral monitoring, pricing, loan-level transparency, risk systems, and compliance tools. Finally, it addresses coordination with investment managers, position visibility and restrictions, recalls, corporate actions, income collection, recall timing, and efforts to prevent sell fails and overdrafts.

nodes.title: L. (At SBCERS Option) Benefit Payment Services
nodes.summary: The section requests information about the firm’s benefit payment services: distinguishing strengths, organizational unit, service history, pension-plan clients and recent additions or terminations, staffing and retirement credentials, and 2023 periodic and lump-sum payment volumes and assets, including check versus ACH/EFT percentages. It asks about processing timelines, advance funding and coordination with custodial services, a 2024 FTP cutoff calendar, quality and security controls, and systems integration with custodial accounting and reporting. It also covers online access for SBCERS staff and pensioners, participant self-service features, beneficiary-change processing and authentication controls, and online and phone support for pensioners and staff.

nodes.title: M. Transition and Conversion Planning Incumbent only needs to respond to the first two questions.
nodes.summary: The text lists SBCERS RFP questions on transition and conversion planning: incumbent benefits and service changes; deconversion support, records, reconciliation, research, and fees; transition-team members, roles, biographies, and relationship to the service team; formal planning, sample documents, timelines, and differences from a typical transition; moving markets to the bidder’s sub-custody network, problem markets, risks, costs, and mitigations; training for SBCERS, managers, custodians, agents, depositories, and securities-lending providers; a comparable conversion, client resource needs, lead time, team involvement, systems and data preparation, parallel processing, accruals, accounting and valuation, asset transfer controls, tax-reclaim loading and reconciliation, and recent BNY Mellon transition references. The appendix requests pricing for two required unit-price scenarios—with and without securities lending—including executable-form fee schedules and assumptions. Scenario 1 assumes lending and asks for service fees, revenue split, collateral-reinvestment fee, estimated gross revenue, and restrictions. Tables cover base fees, renegotiation triggers, and asset-based custody/accounting rates across US and listed international markets, with supplied asset volumes and unit-price, unit, and calculated-fee fields.

result.title: 07_SBCERS Custody RFP - Appendix 4 - Price Proposal
result.summary: Appendix 4 is SBCERS’s pricing proposal for global custody and related services. Bidders must quote all in-scope services using unit prices for both scenarios—with and without securities lending—and submit contract-ready fee schedules with assumptions, disclaimers, supporting documents, and proposed terms. The form covers base fees and material-change provisions that may trigger renegotiation; asset-based custody/accounting charges for U.S. and international markets; STIF investment fees; transaction charges for securities, funds, wires, futures, margin, transfers, and FX; FX spreads, benchmarks, and other revenue; account-based custody and accounting; performance analytics and compliance; class-action access and claims; and optional limited-partner cash-flow and valuation support. The lending scenario also requests the revenue split, collateral-reinvestment fees, estimated gross lending revenue, and restrictions. Bidders must identify other fees and attach a proposed fee exhibit. The tables provide activity and asset volumes, pricing and calculated-fee fields; displayed fees and totals are generally zero.

nodes.summary: Appendix 4 requests pricing for the SBCERS Global Custody and Related Services RFP. Bidders must price all RFP services under both required unit-price scenarios—with and without securities lending—and provide an executable-form fee schedule with applicable disclaimers, assumptions, and documentation. For the securities-lending scenario, provide fees based on Addendum I, the proposed revenue split, any cash-collateral reinvestment fee, estimated gross revenue using the supplied holdings (after cash rebate and before the split), and any comments or restrictions. The page also includes annual fees for listed services per unit volume, a base fee for services within scope, and material-change clause terms identifying changes in asset size, transactional volume, or account volume that could trigger fee renegotiation.

nodes.title: ASSET BASED CHARGES FOR CUSTODY/ACCOUNTING SERVICES PER SCOPE REQUIREMENTS
nodes.summary: Appendix 4 is a pricing proposal for SBCERS Global Custody and Related Services, requesting asset-based custody/accounting charges using a unit-price approach. It lists US asset categories (including STIF, physical securities, funds/line items, and assets under custody) and numerous international markets, asking bidders to provide rates even where assets are not currently held; additional markets may be added. The table includes asset volumes and fields for client/custodian revenue split, unit price, units, calculated fees in USD, and basis-point rates. Scenario 1 includes securities lending. Bidders must complete both required scenarios—with and without securities lending—and quote all RFP services. For each scenario, they must also provide a contract-execution-format fee schedule containing applicable disclaimers, assumptions, and supporting documentation.

nodes.summary: Appendix 4 is a pricing proposal for SBCERS Global Custody and Related Services, Scenario 1 (with securities lending). It requests unit prices for all RFP services and an execution-ready fee schedule including assumptions, disclaimers, and documentation; a second scenario without lending is also required. Pricing categories include U.S. custody and fund transaction activity (securities, wires, futures, margin, transfers, and FX) and buy/sell transactions across listed international markets, with rates requested for any unpriced markets. It also covers custodial FX standing-instruction spreads and benchmarks, restricted-market spreads, and other transaction charges; custody/accounting fees by account type and service; performance analytics, compliance, benchmarks, characteristics, and attribution; class-action access, claims, and historical filing charges; and optional limited-partner services such as cash-flow processing and valuation support. The tables show activity figures and mostly zero-valued price entries.

The page requests foreign-exchange standing-instruction spread methodology, reference rates and benchmarks, explicit spreads for freely convertible and restricted currencies, and other transaction charges. It requests charges for cash-flow processing (contributions and distributions), quarterly valuation reconciliation (posting, reconciliation, and roll-forward), lagged valuation performance support, and any described other charges, priced per line item per year where specified. The extracted tables contain bps and USD fields, line-item figures, amounts including 39,723,521.00 and 8,315,730.00, and numerous zero-valued entries, including other charges of 0.00. Bidders must quote all RFP services, provide unit-price approaches for both required scenarios—with and without securities lending—and submit an executable-form fee schedule for each, including applicable disclaimers, assumptions, and documentation.

Bidders must price all RFP services, provide both lending and non-lending scenarios, and submit an executable-form fee schedule with assumptions, disclaimers, documentation, and proposed terms. The tables cover base fees and material-change renegotiation factors; custody/accounting asset-based charges for U.S. and listed international markets; STIF investment charges; U.S. and international transaction fees; FX spreads, benchmarks, and other revenue; custody/accounting and performance-analytics account fees; class-action access, claims, and historical filing charges; and optional LP-support services.
